articles.title: Neuralink and Animal Communication
articles.body:
Elon Musk’s Neuralink could one day help humans communicate with animals, as advances in brain implants and artificial intelligence open new possibilities for understanding other species.

Neuralink already allows people with paralysis to control computers using brain signals, while separate research projects like Project CETI and Earth Species Project use AI to study communication among whales, elephants, and other animals. Scientists are identifying patterns in animal sounds, but translating thoughts remains unproven.

Although 2028 has circulated as a possible timeline, Neuralink has not confirmed any plans or release date for animal communication technology. Researchers still face major challenges in understanding what animals actually think and express.

articles.title: A Shape-Shifting Liquid Robot
articles.body:
Scientists in South Korea have developed a shape-shifting liquid robot that looks like something straight out of Terminator 2.

Created by researchers at Seoul National University and Gachon University, the robot uses liquid metal mixed with magnetic particles to switch between flexible and rigid states.

When exposed to a magnetic field, the particles organize into a temporary structure that helps the material hold its shape and withstand pressure. Remove the magnetic field, and it becomes soft and fluid again.

During laboratory experiments, the robot demonstrated its ability to squeeze through tight spaces before regaining its strength and structure. Unlike conventional robots built with mechanical joints, this technology relies on magnetic control and the unique properties of its materials.

Published in Science Advances, the research could open new possibilities for medical robotics, search-and-rescue operations, and exploring environments that traditional machines cannot easily access.

articles.title: Understanding Animal Communication in the Age of AI
articles.body:
Artificial intelligence is giving researchers new tools to study how animals communicate. By examining large collections of sounds, scientists can identify recurring patterns that might otherwise escape human attention. Such patterns, however, do not automatically reveal what an animal is thinking.

Brain-computer interfaces are developing along a separate path. Some systems help people with paralysis interact with computers, but applying these technologies to communication between humans and other species presents different challenges. Researchers must first establish how signals relate to behaviour and context.

Speculation about when interspecies conversations might become possible should therefore be treated with caution. Progress depends on careful experiments and reliable evidence, not simply on the availability of powerful technology.

articles.title: Flexible Materials and the Future of Robotics
articles.body:
Robots are often imagined as machines made of rigid parts. Yet researchers are exploring materials that can change their physical properties in response to external conditions. These materials may eventually allow machines to adapt to environments that ordinary robots find difficult to enter.

One approach combines a flexible material with particles that respond to a magnetic field. Under suitable conditions, the field can help the material hold its shape; without it, the material may become more fluid. This combination could allow a device to pass through a narrow opening and then regain a useful structure.

Potential applications range from medical devices to search-and-rescue equipment. However, promising laboratory demonstrations do not automatically become practical products. Researchers still need to evaluate control, safety and performance in real-world conditions.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about identifying patterns in animal sounds?

options.text: It proves that scientists can translate animal thoughts.
It may assist research, but does not by itself reveal animal thoughts.
